brief: The ninth statue with a calm, steady expression, one hand lifted as if to hold a thought; Śuka checking words on his claws; Dādī nodding; the earlier eight statues behind her in the lamplight; the first stars outside the hall.

The fourth statue holding a polished bronze mirror, in which the three travellers are reflected; Śuka peering into it; Dādī smiling; the earlier three statues behind; Lubdhaka's foreman in the background with a notebook.

The second statue, a woman holding a conch, with Śuka on Dādī's shoulder counting on his claws; Lubdhaka's foreman looking on with arms folded; the first statue beside her with a lotus; morning light on the dig.

A hill above Ujjayinī at dawn: workmen's tents and ropes around a half-uncovered stone throne ringed by thirty-two weathered statues of women; the first statue, holding a lotus, close to the viewer; Lubdhaka's foreman frowning at her; you, Dādī and Śuka at the edge of the dig.
The third statue holding a small drum, her fingers poised to tap; the first two statues beside her; Śuka squinting up at her; Lubdhaka's foreman wiping his brow; morning light.

A poor young man in a patched kurta standing before a richly dressed merchant in a market lane; the merchant looking down at a small dead mouse on the ground and laughing, the young man pointing at it with a thoughtful look; warm old-India watercolour.

The young man at a shady crossroads outside the town with a water pot and a basket of roasted chickpeas, giving them to tired woodcutters who rest under a tree with bundles of logs beside them; late afternoon light.

The young man in good clothes standing proudly at the door of his own busy shop, holding up a small golden mouse; the old merchant Viśākhila smiling beside his daughter who is garlanding him; neighbours cheering.
